deepDive.title: Anthropic's Physical AI Standard Changes the Game
deepDive.html:
Overview

Anthropic has just made its boldest leap yet: a new Model Hardware Standard (MHS) that extends its MCP protocol into the physical world, letting AI agents directly operate lab equipment, industrial machinery, and manufactured hardware. AI has left the screen.

The Details

  • Anthropic unveiled MHS — the hardware counterpart to its software-layer Model Context Protocol (MCP) — enabling AI agents to interface with and control physical machines.
  • Initial use cases target scientists and manufacturers, giving AI agents the ability to autonomously operate lab instruments and industrial hardware.
  • This is Anthropic's first move into physical AI, marking a significant expansion beyond language model applications.
  • Coverage from CNBC, Fortune, and Firstpost today reflects broad industry recognition of its significance.
  • The launch accompanies expanded Anthropic support for scientists, signalling a deliberate push into technical and research domains.

Why It Matters

Physical AI creates a new risk layer financial institutions cannot ignore. Banks operate vast physical infrastructure — data centres, ATM networks, branch automation, secure document handling. The question isn't whether AI agents will start managing hardware, but when. MHS sets the standards today that will govern that future, and risk and compliance teams should be briefing boards now.

For insurers and asset managers, the implications are more immediate. When AI agents can cause physical harm or operational failures, new liability categories emerge that existing policies don't cover. Asset managers with industrial or manufacturing holdings should model the upside — and the fresh tail risks — that physical AI agents introduce across their portfolio companies.

items.tagline: AI agent platform helping small businesses automate operations and growth
items.summary: Runable closed a $21M Series A led by Susquehanna and Nexus, reaching 1.5 million users and $2M ARR. Funds will expand growth channels and its free AI academy.
items.analysis: **SME market signal.** Runable's scale with 1.5M users shows AI agents penetrating the SME segment fast — banks serving small business clients should watch for disintermediation of their advisory and operational banking services.

items.tagline: Identity verification and AI-powered fraud investigation platform for financial institutions
items.summary: Socure secured $156M at a $5.2B valuation and acquired Fravity, an AI fraud investigation startup, integrating agentic fraud detection into its identity verification stack.
items.analysis: **Fraud automation escalating.** Socure's acquisition signals that fraud investigation — historically labour-intensive — is now a target for full AI automation; banks still relying on manual fraud review face a growing competitive and cost disadvantage.

items.headline: Focus: As AI agents go rogue, cyber insurers are adapting their policies
items.summary: Cyber insurers are revising policies as autonomous AI agents that take harmful or unintended actions expose major gaps in existing coverage. The industry is moving to redefine terms before losses mount.
items.keyPoint: **Coverage gap now.** Banks deploying autonomous AI agents should urgently verify whether their cyber policies extend to losses caused by rogue agent behaviour — insurers are already tightening terms.

items.headline: OutSystems debuts Agentic Loan Applications for banks
items.summary: OutSystems has launched agentic loan application tooling built specifically for banks, enabling AI agents to handle core stages of the loan origination process autonomously.
items.keyPoint: **Loan ops disruption.** Enterprise-grade agentic tools for banking are moving from pilots to deployment — institutions that delay automation in lending risk falling behind on speed and cost efficiency.

items.headline: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and 100 other companies call for action to defend against rogue AI
items.summary: Over 100 major tech companies and AI labs jointly called for stronger cybersecurity measures to combat rogue AI threats, declaring current defences inadequate and advertising a new solution.
items.keyPoint: **Systemic threat signal.** A 100-company coalition raising the alarm means financial institutions should treat AI-driven cyberattacks as a top-tier risk category — not a theoretical edge case.

items.headline: Hong Kong expands AI sandbox with new projects spanning dozens of partners
items.summary: Hong Kong has expanded its AI sandbox initiative, bringing dozens of partners into AI application testing for financial services, reinforcing its position as a leading APAC hub for regulated AI experimentation.
items.keyPoint: **APAC governance race.** Hong Kong and Singapore are competing to set AI rules for financial services — institutions operating across APAC should engage with sandbox programmes now to shape emerging frameworks.

items.headline: Lucie Money and Fiskil Partner to Launch AI Money Agent Powered by Open Banking
items.summary: Lucie Money has partnered with Fiskil to launch an AI money agent that uses open banking data to deliver personalised financial guidance and automated money management for consumers.
items.keyPoint: **Open banking AI convergence.** Pairing open banking data rails with AI agents creates a new class of proactive financial assistant — incumbents should note this model threatens advisory relationships, not just transaction fees.
